POL-580.title: IMPLEMENT: finish Polaris execution adapter / governance wiring
POL-580.body:
## Objective

Close the five governance gaps in the Paperclip execution adapter identified by [POL-579](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-579/analyze-finish-polaris-execution-adapter-governance-wiring)'s analysis.

## Context

Analysis: `smartdocs/raw/analysis/pol-579-paperclip-adapter-governance-analysis.md`. Source ANALYZE issue: [POL-579](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-579/analyze-finish-polaris-execution-adapter-governance-wiring). Adapter code at `src/loop/adapters/paperclip.ts` is verified byte-identical between this repo and the Polaris-CLO VPS runtime host.

## Goal

`PaperclipAdapter` supports per-role assignee resolution (with `reportsTo` fallback), only reports a child as done when a verifiable work product exists, is proven to flow through the same QC/medic/librarian pipeline as every other adapter, and routes reusable sub-work through Polaris skills.

## Scope

Cluster-wide allowed paths (each child scopes further):

* src/config/schema.ts
* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.ts
* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.test.ts
* src/loop/adapters/**tests**/paperclip.test.ts
* src/loop/parent.ts
* src/loop/lifecycle-dispatch.ts
* test/**

## Acceptance Criteria

* roleBindings + reportsTo config is additive and optional (existing configs behave identically unset).
* A Paperclip child is only marked done when a linked PR/commit/branch/work-product is present.
* Test coverage proves paperclip dispatch results are treated identically to terminal-cli by QC/medic/librarian.
* Issue body sent to Paperclip includes a role→skill routing block.
* No changes outside this repo (no Paperclip source, no hermes profile files).

## Validation

* npm run build
* npm test
* npx vitest run src/loop/adapters

## Ordering

See clusters.json — children execute in dependency order within one cluster.

## Non-goals

* No changes to Paperclip source code or the hermes worker profile.
* No new secret-handling path outside `PaperclipExecutionConfig.tokenEnv`.
* No cross-agent delegation policy changes beyond this adapter.

POL-585.title: Add role→skill routing block to paperclip issue body builder
POL-585.body:
## Objective

Give Paperclip agents an explicit pointer to which Polaris skill/command reusable sub-work should be delegated through, instead of only raw steps/scope text.

## Context

`mapBootstrapPacketToPaperclipIssue()` (`src/loop/adapters/paperclip.ts:177-308`) builds the issue body from `instructions.steps`, `allowed_scope`, and `validation_commands`, plus a raw packet JSON dump. It has no concept of Polaris skill routing, so a Paperclip agent reading the issue has no signal that reusable sub-work (e.g. another analyze/run cycle) should go through a named Polaris skill/command rather than being done inline.

## Goal

Add a routing block to the generated issue body mapping the child's `worker_role` (already resolved by `workerRoleFromPacket()`) to the Polaris skill/command name it corresponds to (e.g. `analyst` → `polaris-analyze`, `worker` → `polaris-run`), sourced from a small static role→skill table colocated with the adapter (not a new config surface — keep this additive and simple per the config-first-rollback constraint). Include this block in the description alongside the existing sections.

## Scope

* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.ts
* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.test.ts
* src/loop/adapters/**tests**/paperclip.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

* Issue body includes a clearly labeled role→skill routing section when the role has a known mapping.
* Unknown/unmapped roles omit the section rather than emitting a placeholder — no behavior change for roles with no mapping.
* Existing issue-body snapshot/assertion tests are updated to account for the new section, not broken by it.

## Validation

* npm run build
* npm test
* npx vitest run src/loop/adapters

## Ordering

* Depends on [POL-582](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-582/wire-role-aware-assignee-resolution-into-paperclip-adapter-dispatch) (reuses `workerRoleFromPacket()`/role resolution wiring landed there).

## Non-goals

* Do not implement actual skill dispatch from Paperclip's side — this child only adds the routing hint to the issue body; Paperclip's own agent is responsible for acting on it.

POL-584.title: Prove paperclip dispatch results flow through the same QC/medic/librarian pipeline as other adapters
POL-584.body:
## Objective

Confirm — and fix if false — that a `DispatchResult` produced by `PaperclipAdapter` is consumed identically to one from any other adapter by the QC → medic → librarian → PR-gate pipeline.

## Context

Grepping `src/loop/lifecycle-dispatch.ts`, `src/loop/parent.ts`, `src/qc/`, `src/medic/`, `src/finalize/` for `"paperclip"` today only turns up assignee/provider-selection special-casing in `parent.ts:968-1020` (choosing the paperclip provider and its selection_reason) — no skip of QC/medic/librarian was found for the paperclip path specifically. This child turns that grep-based observation into an enforced, tested guarantee rather than an assumption, and closes any gap found.

## Goal

Add a test (or tests) that dispatches through `PaperclipAdapter` (using the existing mock-server test harness in `paperclip.test.ts`) and asserts the resulting `DispatchResult` is handed to the same downstream QC/medic/librarian code path in `src/loop/parent.ts` / `src/loop/lifecycle-dispatch.ts` as a `terminal-cli` dispatch result would be — no adapter-name branch skips it. If a gap is found during this work, fix it in the same child (small, scoped fix only; if the fix is large, stop and report instead of expanding scope).

## Scope

* src/loop/parent.ts
* src/loop/lifecycle-dispatch.ts
* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.test.ts
* src/loop/adapters/**tests**/paperclip.test.ts
* test/** (integration-level dispatch pipeline tests, if that's where this is best asserted)

## Acceptance Criteria

* A test explicitly proves paperclip-sourced `DispatchResult`s reach QC/medic/librarian the same way terminal-cli ones do.
* If no gap exists, the test passes as a regression guard (no production code change needed).
* If a gap exists, it is fixed and the same test proves the fix.

## Validation

* npm run build
* npm test
* npx vitest run src/loop

## Ordering

* Depends on [POL-583](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-583/gate-paperclip-done-disposition-on-verifiable-work-product-evidence) (evidence-gated disposition must land first so the "done" results reaching this pipeline are trustworthy).

## Non-goals

* Do not redesign the QC/medic/librarian pipeline itself — this child only proves/fixes paperclip's participation in the existing one.

POL-583.title: Gate paperclip done-disposition on verifiable work-product evidence
POL-583.body:
## Objective

Stop the adapter from trusting Paperclip's own `status: "done"` as sufficient evidence of completion.

## Context

`waitForPaperclipExecution()` (`src/loop/adapters/paperclip.ts:542-570`) polls `getPaperclipIssue()` and returns as soon as Paperclip's `status` is `done`/`cancelled`/`failed`/`blocked`. `dispatch()` (`paperclip.ts:587-696`) then returns `exit_code: 0` purely on `status: "done"` — no check for a linked PR, commit, branch, or other work product. Paperclip's own agent-facing protocol (fetched from the VPS host's `AGENTS.md`) explicitly warns that "comments, documents, screenshots, work products, and `Remaining` bullets are evidence, not valid liveness paths by themselves" and expects a `pull_request`/`commit`/`branch` work product for operator-facing deliverables — this child makes the Polaris side actually check for that.

## Goal

Before `dispatch()` returns `exit_code: 0` for a `status: "done"` issue, verify via `getPaperclipIssue()` (or a new typed field on its response, if the current response type doesn't expose work products/attachments) that at least one PR/commit/branch/work-product reference exists. If none is found, return a failure result (`exit_code: 2`, `failure_category` describing missing evidence) instead of success.

## Scope

* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.ts
* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.test.ts
* src/loop/adapters/**tests**/paperclip.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

* `status: "done"` with a linked PR/commit/branch/work-product still returns `exit_code: 0`.
* `status: "done"` with no such evidence returns a non-zero exit code and a descriptive failure message — the run does not silently advance.
* `status: "blocked"`/`"cancelled"`/`"failed"` behavior is unchanged (already surfaced as non-success today, per existing tests).
* If `getPaperclipIssue()`'s current response type doesn't expose enough structured data to detect evidence, extend its typing/parsing rather than parsing free-text comments; note this as a risk if the Paperclip API turns out not to expose it at all, and report back instead of guessing at an undocumented field.

## Validation

* npm run build
* npm test
* npx vitest run src/loop/adapters

## Ordering

* None — independent of [POL-581](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-581/add-rolebindings-reportsto-fallback-to-paperclipexecutionconfig-schema)/[POL-582](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-582/wire-role-aware-assignee-resolution-into-paperclip-adapter-dispatch) (different code path within the same file; safe to land in parallel or before/after).

## Non-goals

* Do not change `src/finalize/delivery-integrity.ts` — that check remains as a separate, later safety net.

POL-582.title: Wire role-aware assignee resolution into paperclip adapter dispatch
POL-582.body:
## Objective

Make the Paperclip adapter assign issues based on the dispatched child's role instead of a single static agent.

## Context

`workerRoleFromPacket()` (`src/loop/adapters/paperclip.ts:157`) already extracts a `worker_role` string from the bootstrap packet, but `mapBootstrapPacketToPaperclipIssue()` (`paperclip.ts:177`) never uses it — it always falls back to `config.assigneeAgentId`. [POL-581](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-581/add-rolebindings-reportsto-fallback-to-paperclipexecutionconfig-schema) adds `roleBindings`/`reportsTo` to the config schema; this child consumes them.

## Goal

Add `resolveAssigneeForRole(role: string, config: PaperclipRuntimeConfig): string` that:

1. Returns `roleBindings[role]` if present.
2. Otherwise follows `reportsTo[role]` (one hop, or a bounded chain with cycle detection) to find a binding.
3. Falls back to `config.assigneeAgentId` if no binding resolves.

Wire this into `mapBootstrapPacketToPaperclipIssue()` in place of the current direct `config.assigneeAgentId` read.

## Scope

* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.ts
* src/loop/adapters/paperclip.test.ts
* src/loop/adapters/**tests**/paperclip.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

* Role with a direct `roleBindings` entry resolves to that assignee.
* Role with no direct binding but a `reportsTo` chain resolves to the fallback's assignee.
* Role with neither resolves to `config.assigneeAgentId` (today's behavior, unchanged).
* A `reportsTo` cycle does not infinite-loop — resolution terminates and falls back to `assigneeAgentId`.
* Existing tests without `roleBindings` configured still pass unmodified.

## Validation

* npm run build
* npm test
* npx vitest run src/loop/adapters

## Ordering

* Depends on [POL-581](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-581/add-rolebindings-reportsto-fallback-to-paperclipexecutionconfig-schema) (schema fields must exist first).

## Non-goals

* Do not change how `executionBlock.assigneeAgentId` (per-packet override, if present) is prioritized relative to role resolution — preserve existing precedence, just extend the fallback chain beneath it.

POL-581.title: Add roleBindings + reportsTo fallback to PaperclipExecutionConfig schema
POL-581.body:
## Objective

Add an additive, optional role→assignee mapping to the Paperclip execution config schema.

## Context

`PaperclipExecutionConfig` (`src/config/schema.ts:214-244`) currently has a single static `assigneeAgentId`. [POL-579](https://linear.app/lsctech/issue/POL-579/analyze-finish-polaris-execution-adapter-governance-wiring)'s analysis found no `roleBindings` or `reportsTo` field anywhere in config or loop code, so every role is assigned to the same Paperclip agent. This mirrors the existing `RoleProviderPolicy` additive-schema pattern from `provider-role-dispatch-governance.md`.

## Goal

`PaperclipExecutionConfig` gains:

* `roleBindings?: Record<string, string>` — maps a worker role (e.g. `"worker"`, `"analyst"`, `"librarian"`) to a Paperclip `assigneeAgentId`.
* `reportsTo?: Record<string, string>` — optional org-chain fallback: maps a role to another role whose binding should be used when the role itself has no direct binding.

Both fields are optional. Omitting them reproduces today's behavior (always uses the top-level `assigneeAgentId`) exactly.

## Scope

* src/config/schema.ts
* src/config/schema.json (if present and mirrors schema.ts)
* test/config/** or equivalent schema validator tests

## Acceptance Criteria

* `roleBindings` and `reportsTo` are typed and optional on `PaperclipExecutionConfig`.
* Config validator accepts configs with and without the new fields.
* A test fixture with `roleBindings`/`reportsTo` populated passes validation.
* No runtime behavior changes in this child — schema only.

## Validation

* npm run build
* npm test

## Ordering

* None — first child, no dependencies.

## Non-goals

* Do not wire the new fields into `paperclip.ts` dispatch logic (next child).
